We chose the mental health inpatient activity data. Our ideas are revolving around joining two or more datasets in order to find a relationship between several variables, e.g. how do different variables (age, diagnosis, hospital) affect the length of stay?

During our first workshop we had the idea of joining the data by diagnosis, since it will exclude any patients with missing diagnosis, and also provide the patients' characteristics.

Initial ideas:

-   Number of patients in each age range  

    -   Percentage of male and female in each age range

-   Length of stay and diagnosis for each age range / sex

    -   Would health beliefs impact length of stay/diagnosis?

    -   Would area of admission impact length of stay/diagnosis?

-   How has awareness of mental health evolved over time?

    -   Frequency of stays

-   Number of admissions during each year/time period

    -   What external factors would effect this?

    -   Percentage of male/females. Did numbers change over time? Did men become more accepting to health care?

    -   Percentage of age ranges. Did numbers change over time?
    
-  How has the treatment for mental health changed between 1997/98 and 2021/22
    - merge the relevant data sets to get a more complete view 
    
    count of patients - y axis and then barchart, each bar is one year
    whole of scotland, either look at financial year or age group 
    
    1) take only 2 financial years, look at the count of patients of each sex in each age range. then make box plot for lenght of stay. then look at diagnosis of each. 
    one graph, x axis age group, y axis would be patient count and then make bar chart of two different colours in each bar represeting male and female.

```{r load-data}
# Load your data
mental_health_inpatient_activity_age_sex <- read_csv("data/mental-health-inpatient-activity-age-sex.csv")
y97_98<-filter(mental_health_inpatient_activity_age_sex,FinancialYear=="1997/98")
y21_22<-filter(mental_health_inpatient_activity_age_sex,FinancialYear=="2021/22")
plot1<-ggplot(y97_98,aes(fill=Sex,y=PatientsCount,x=AgeGroup))+geom_bar(position="dodge",stat="identity")+ labs(title = "Patient distribution by sex in 1997/98 in different age groups",
       x = "Age Groups", 
       y = "Number of Patients")
plot2<-ggplot(y21_22,aes(fill=Sex,y=PatientsCount,x=AgeGroup))+geom_bar(position="dodge",stat="identity")+labs(title = "Patient distribution by sex in 2021/22 in different age groups",
       x = "Age Groups", 
       y = "Number of Patients")
plot1
plot2

#ggplot(new_df1,aes(fill=Sex,y=PatientsCount,x=AgeGroup))+geom_bar(position="dodge",stat="identity")

age.sex <- read_csv("data/mental-health-inpatient-activity-age-sex.csv")
length.of.stay <- read_csv("data/mental-health-inpatient-activity-length-of-stay.csv")

#Bar chart for age.sex
age.sex %>% filter(HBR == "S92000003") %>%
            group_by(FinancialYear, Sex) %>%
            summarise(amount = sum(PatientsCount)) %>%
            ggplot(aes(x = FinancialYear, y = amount, fill = Sex)) +
            geom_col() +
            theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45))

length.of.stay %>% filter(HBT == "S92000003") %>%
            group_by(FinancialYear, LengthOfStay) %>%
            summarise(amount = sum(NumberOfStays)) %>%
            ggplot(aes(x = FinancialYear, y = amount, fill = LengthOfStay)) +
            geom_col() +
            theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45))



```
